title: ghent-live · morning review
subtitle: Ghent's historic centre in 3D, built overnight (master PR #36). Every step opens a view by its URL hash on the app you have open; the small committed samples load unless a step says **live**. Pin a note with **Reviewer → Add comment** wherever something looks wrong: the note carries the exact view.

features.title: The stage view: Street level at night
features.intro: The opening shot of the talk: from the Sint-Michielsbrug, the three towers in a row, lit, with a parking answer on the right.
steps: Open the view. You stand on the bridge at eye height, looking east along the Korenmarkt.
Look for **Sint-Niklaas**, the **Belfort** (with its spire) and **Sint-Baafs**, left to right, each lit warm orange against a dark city, each with its name label.
The **Ask Ghent** panel on the right answers *Where should I park to reach Gravensteen?* with a garage and a percentage; the Sint-Baafs label stays visible beside it.
The street and the buildings stay dark; the towers are the brightest thing in the frame. No red beam stands in the sky.
features.pass: Three lit towers with their three labels, and a parking answer in the panel, all readable from the back of a room.

features.title: Buildings at their real heights
features.intro: The default view from the south-west, with the Belfry selected.
steps: Open the view: dense blocks of buildings of different heights fill the centre.
The Belfry stands at the red ring, highlighted in magenta, its spire clearly above the roofs; a thin red beam rises from the ring.
Click any other building: it turns magenta and the URL's `sel` becomes `bldg:<number>`.
features.pass: The Belfry rises clearly above the roofs at the red ring, and clicking a building selects it.

features.title: Ground, water and streets
features.intro: The city from straight above, north up.
steps: Open the view. The Leie and the Schelde run through the map as continuous blue bands, never covered by the coloured zones.
The streets form an irregular medieval pattern; no square grid shows anywhere.
Switch **Circulation** off in the Layers panel: the bare land, streets and water stay; switch it back on.
features.pass: The rivers read as water through the zones, and the streets are the real, irregular street plan.

features.title: The circulation plan
features.intro: The 2017 circulation plan: sectors around a car-free core, and the knips where cars cannot pass.
steps: Open the view. Coloured sectors surround a pale car-free core (**Kuip**, selected with a white outline); neighbouring sectors differ in colour.
Small red posts (the knips) stand on the sector borders.
Sector names (Coupure, Portus Ganda, Krook, …) show in large text and never overlap a landmark label.
features.pass: Zones, the car-free core and the knips are all visible, and the streets still read through the zones.

features.title: The Lichtplan by night and by day
features.intro: The city's night lighting: lit towers and a glowing walk.
steps: Open the view. Warm lights shine on the towers and the facades; a glowing walk runs through the streets.
Click **Day** in the panel on the left: the walk becomes a thin dashed line with small markers, and nothing glows.
Click **Night** again: the lights come back.
features.pass: At night the towers are lit and the walk glows; by day nothing glows.

features.title: Parking garages, live
features.intro: One column per garage in the centre: its height is the capacity, its solid part the occupied places, its colour the share still free.
steps: Open the view (samples). Columns of different heights stand in the city; the Vrijdagmarkt column is highlighted with a label giving its free places.
The columns stay well below the three towers.

Open the [live view](/#cam=420,310,-820&tgt=-150,30,30&sel=garage:vrijdagmarkt&mode=live): the page reloads with the city's current feed, and the status line under the title says so if the data is more than 15 minutes old.
features.pass: Five garages show as partly filled columns, and the live view draws the current occupancy.

features.title: Shared bikes, live
features.intro: One thin bar per shared-bike station, its height the bikes available, one colour per operator (Donkey Republic orange, Bolt green).
steps: Open the view (samples). Thin bars stand along the streets, also behind the roofs (drawn through them, fainter, from this height); most are short stubs.
Click a bar: it turns white and wider, and the URL's `sel` becomes `bikes:<operator>:<id>`.
Open the [live view](/#cam=-230,110,370&tgt=0,0,-20&mode=live): about 110 Donkey Republic and 700 Bolt stations inside the area; most Bolt stations show 0 bikes.
features.pass: The bars read along the streets in two colours, and a click selects a station.

features.title: Ask Ghent
features.intro: Typed questions about the city's state, answered on the server; the key never reaches the browser.
steps: Open the view: the panel answers *Is the centre busy right now?* with Yes or No and a percentage.

steps.text: Type this question in the panel and press **Ask**; the answer arrives within a second or two:

copy.label: Question
copy.text: Can I drive from Coupure to Portus Ganda without leaving the R40 ring road?

steps: Click **×**: the question clears and the panel folds to a small **Ask Ghent** button; click it to open the panel again.

Open the [live parking question](/#cam=-212.1,230,252.8&tgt=0,40,0&ask=park:gravensteen&mode=live): the answer names a garage drawn on the map and highlights it; if the Bolt feed is stale, a line in the panel says Bolt bikes were left out.
features.pass: Each question gets an answer with a percentage, and a parking answer highlights a garage that is drawn.

features.title: Camera, labels and controls
features.intro: Six camera presets with a smooth flight, layer switches, the day/night switch and landmark labels, all large enough for a projector and usable by touch.
steps: Open the view (**From above**). Landmark labels name the Belfort, Sint-Baafs, Gravensteen and others; no two labels overlap, and none touches a panel.
Click each preset along the bottom: **Belfort**, **Graslei**, **Gravensteen**, **Sint-Baafs**, **Street level**. Each flight is smooth and never goes under the street.
Drag to orbit at Street level: the camera may look a little up at the towers but never sinks below the street.
The attribution line under the preset buttons stays readable.
features.pass: Every preset flies smoothly to a readable view, and the labels never cover each other or the controls.

features.title: Review in the app
features.intro: A note pinned here reaches the agent with the exact view and a screenshot.
steps: Open the view: the default camera at night, the Belfry selected.
Click **Reviewer**, then **Add comment**, share the tab when the browser asks, click the red ring and send a short note.
The note is confirmed as sent; the agent replies with the view it opened from the note's URL.
features.pass: The note arrives with its comment, the view's URL and a screenshot with the pin.
